source: Because Nav1.7–Nav1.9 are predominantly expressed in neurons of DRG and trigeminal ganglia, and are crucial for pain perception and transmission (Cummins et al., 2004; Cox et al., 2006; Huang et al., 2014; Dib-Hajj et al., 2015; Huang et al., 2013; Cummins et al., 2007; Dib-Hajj et al., 2010)
evidence: This is a background claim supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Nav1.7–Nav1.9 are crucial for pain perception and transmission.
source: Because Nav1.7–Nav1.9 are predominantly expressed in neurons of DRG and trigeminal ganglia, and are crucial for pain perception and transmission (Cummins et al., 2004; Cox et al., 2006; Huang et al., 2014; Dib-Hajj et al., 2015; Huang et al., 2013; Cummins et al., 2007; Dib-Hajj et al., 2010)
evidence: This is a background claim supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: A-type FHFs induce INaR via the N-terminus by a relief-of-open-channel-block mechanism, similar to the mechanism proposed for the Navβ4 peptide-dependent INaR.
source: These similarities lead us to propose that A-type FHFs induce INaR via the N-terminus by a relief-of-open-channel-block mechanism, similar to the mechanism proposed for the Navβ4 peptide-dependent INaR (Lewis and Raman, 2014).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the experimental data and a citation to Lewis and Raman, 2014.

claim: FHF4 knockout accelerates the onset of fast inactivation of sodium currents in cerebellar Purkinje neurons.
source: Interestingly, FHF4 knockout accelerates the onset of fast inactivation of sodium currents (White et al., 2019) and hyperpolarizes the voltage dependence of sodium current inactivation (Bosch et al., 2015) in cerebellar Purkinje neurons.
evidence: This is a background claim supported by a citation to White et al., 2019.

claim: FHF4 knockout hyperpolarizes the voltage dependence of sodium current inactivation in cerebellar Purkinje neurons.
source: Interestingly, FHF4 knockout accelerates the onset of fast inactivation of sodium currents (White et al., 2019) and hyperpolarizes the voltage dependence of sodium current inactivation (Bosch et al., 2015) in cerebellar Purkinje neurons.
evidence: This is a background claim supported by a citation to Bosch et al., 2015.

claim: A-type FHFs induce long-term inactivation of Nav1.6 and Nav1.5.
source: While neither full-length Navβ4 nor full-length FHF4A has been shown to induce Nav1.6 INaR in heterologous expression systems, our data show that FHF4A can induce long-term inactivation of Nav1.6 in ND7/23 cells (Figure 10), which is consistent with previous studies demonstrating that A-type FHFs induce long-term inactivation of Nav1.6 and Nav1.5 (Dover et al., 2010; Yan et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2016; Barbosa et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a background claim supported by citations to Dover et al., 2010; Yan et al., 2014; Yang et al., 2016; Barbosa et al., 2017.

claim: A-type FHF N-terminus may bind more strongly to Nav1.6 and some other VGSCs than to Nav1.8 and Nav1.9.
source: One possible explanation for the induction of long-term inactivation versus the induction of INaR generation is that A-type FHF N-terminus may bind more strongly to Nav1.6 and some other VGSCs than to Nav1.8 and Nav1.9.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism underlying the differential effects of A-type FHFs on different VGSC isoforms.

claim: During repolarization, the driving force is only powerful enough to repel and unbind A-type FHF N-terminus from Nav1.8 and Nav1.9, but not from Nav1.6.
source: During repolarization, the driving force is only powerful enough to repel and unbind A-type FHF N-terminus from Nav1.8 and Nav1.9, but not from Nav1.6, and thus induces robust INaR from Nav1.8 and Nav1.9, but long-term inactivation in Nav1.6.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanism underlying the differential effects of A-type FHFs on different VGSC isoforms.

claim: Post-translational modifications of either Nav1.6 or FHF4A may allow FHF4A to directly induce INaR in Nav1.6 in specific neuronal populations such as cerebellar Purkinje neurons.
source: However, we cannot rule out the possibility that post-translational modifications of either Nav1.6 or FHF4A allows FHF4A to directly induce INaR in Nav1.6, rather than inducing long-term inactivation, in specific neuronal populations such as cerebellar Purkinje neurons.
evidence: This is a speculation about alternative mechanisms that could explain the differential effects of FHF4A on Nav1.6 in different cell types.

claim: F4A peptide at up to 1 mM is required to fully induce the same level of INaR as those induced by full-length FHF4A.
source: Our data show that F4A peptide at up to 1 mM, a nonphysiological concentration, is required to fully induce the same level of INaR as those induced by full-length FHF4A.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figures 3 and 6.

claim: The concentration of F4A peptide required to induce INaR is 5-fold to 10-fold higher than that of Navβ4 peptide (100–200 µM).
source: This concentration is 5-fold to 10-fold higher than that of Navβ4 peptide (100–200 µM) that is required to reconstitute TTX-sensitive INaR.
evidence: This is a comparison claim based on the experimental data.

claim: The β-trefoil core does not directly generate INaR, but it is likely crucial to facilitating INaR generation induced by N-terminus residues in A-type FHFs.
source: The β-trefoil core does not directly generate INaR, but it is likely crucial to facilitating INaR generation induced by N-terminus residues in A-type FHFs, as the core binding to the cytoplasmic tail of VGSCs (Liu et al., 2001; Goetz et al., 2009) would greatly raise the local concentration of the N-terminus near the channel pore.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and citations to Liu et al., 2001; Goetz et al., 2009.

claim: The β-trefoil domain shifts the voltage dependence of steady-state inactivation in the positive direction, augmenting the 'window currents' region.
source: In addition, our data and that of others demonstrate that the β-trefoil domain shifts the voltage dependence of steady-state inactivation in the positive direction, augmenting the 'window currents' region (see Figure 1b and d)
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1b and d.

claim: Open-channel blockers might have higher affinity in VGSCs with DIVS4 deployed than with DIVS4 in the resting or partially deployed configuration.
source: Lewis and Raman, 2013 showed that open-channel blockers might have higher affinity in VGSCs with DIVS4 deployed than with DIVS4 in the resting or partially deployed configuration.
evidence: This is a background claim supported by a citation to Lewis and Raman, 2013.

claim: The molecular manipulation of INaR might be achieved by inhibiting the interaction of A-type FHF β-trefoil core with VGSC C-terminus.
source: This also suggests that the molecular manipulation of INaR might be achieved by inhibiting the interaction of A-type FHF β-trefoil core with VGSC C-terminus.
evidence: This is a speculation about potential therapeutic strategies based on the findings.

claim: A-type FHFs exert various impact on neuronal excitability by differentially modulating the activities of VGSC isoforms.
source: Overall, our work substantially increases understanding of the role of A-type FHFs in sensory neuron excitability. We show that A-type FHFs exert various impact on neuronal excitability by differentially modulating the activities of VGSC isoforms.
evidence: This is a summary claim of the findings of the study.

claim: The accumulation of long-term inactivation seems to be the predominant effect of A-type FHFs on TTX-sensitive VGSC isoforms.
source: The accumulation of long-term inactivation seems to be the predominant effect of A-type FHFs on TTX-sensitive VGSC isoforms, although FHF-mediated INaR (only 0.3% of transient peak current) are inducible with some TTX-sensitive isoforms (Figure 9c and f).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data shown in Figure 9c and f.

claim: By promoting long-term inactivation, FHF2A accumulatively decreases TTX-sensitive sodium currents (e.g., Nav1.6, Nav1.7) by >20%.
source: By promoting long-term inactivation, FHF2A accumulatively decreases TTX-sensitive sodium currents (e.g., Nav1.6, Nav1.7) by >20% (Venkatesan et al., 2014; Effraim et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a background claim supported by citations to Venkatesan et al., 2014; Effraim et al., 2019.

claim: A-type FHFs reduced action potential firing in hippocampal neurons, cerebellar granule neurons, and medium-sized DRG neurons.
source: Prior studies demonstrated that A-type FHFs reduced action potential firing in hippocampal neurons, cerebellar granule neurons (Dover et al., 2010; Venkatesan et al., 2014), and medium-sized DRG neurons, where Nav1.6 channels are predominantly expressed (Barbosa et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a background claim supported by citations to Dover et al., 2010; Venkatesan et al., 2014; Barbosa et al., 2017.

claim: Nav1.8 and Nav1.9 are two TTX-resistant subtypes mainly expressed in nociceptive sensory neurons.
source: Nav1.8 and Nav1.9 are two TTX-resistant subtypes mainly expressed in nociceptive sensory neurons (Fang et al., 2002; Cummins et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a background claim supported by citations to Fang et al., 2002; Cummins et al., 2007.

claim: A-type FHF-mediated INaR significantly upregulate excitability of nociceptive DRG neurons.
source: In Figure 6, we demonstrate that A-type FHF-mediated INaR significantly upregulate excitability of nociceptive DRG neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: A-type FHF-mediated INaR result in broader action potentials and higher firing frequency in nociceptive DRG neurons.
source: The INaR also result in broader action potentials and higher firing frequency.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The T790A variant identified in the Possum transgenic mouse strain leads to increased INaR and enhanced excitability in Nav1.8-transfected DRG neurons.
source: These observations are similar to those detected in Nav1.8 T790A-transfected DRG neurons, in which the T790A variant identified in the Possum transgenic mouse strain leads to increased INaR and enhanced excitability (Xiao et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a background claim supported by a citation to Xiao et al., 2019.

claim: Nav1.8/Nav1.9 have been colocalized with A-type FHFs within trigeminal ganglion neurons, myenteric neurons, magnocellular neurosecretory cells of the supraoptic nucleus, the outer layers of the substantia gelatinosa, and cerebellar neurons in animal models of multiple sclerosis.
source: In addition to DRG neurons, Nav1.8/Nav1.9 have been colocalized with A-type FHFs within other neuronal populations, such as trigeminal ganglion neurons, myenteric neurons, magnocellular neurosecretory cells of the supraoptic nucleus, the outer layers of the substantia gelatinosa, and cerebellar neurons in animal models of multiple sclerosis (Craner et al., 2003; Vohra et al., 2006; Heanue and Pachnis, 2006; Huang et al., 2014; Osorio et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a background claim supported by citations to Craner et al., 2003; Vohra et al., 2006; Heanue and Pachnis, 2006; Huang et al., 2014; Osorio et al., 2014.
